groups.label: Locked
groups.note: Booked and paid. Nothing to do but turn up.

groups.label: This week
groups.note: Already on sale, or needs a human to write back. Waiting only makes these harder.

groups.label: Around 23 September
groups.note: Not bookable yet. Put a reminder in your phone.

groups.label: Early October
groups.note: Short booking horizons. Too early and they will not take the reservation.

groups.label: Checks before you fly
groups.note: Five minutes each, and each one prevents a wasted walk.

groups.label: Needs nothing
groups.note: Walk-ins and pay-at-the-gate, so they can absorb a day that runs late. Watch closing times, not booking windows.

items.title: Flights
items.summary: JL001 out, JL002 home. Seats assigned.
items.detail: JL001 SFO to Haneda, Fri 16 Oct 11:55, landing 15:05 on the 17th, seats 49D and 49E. JL002 Haneda to SFO, Sun 25 Oct 17:55, arriving 11:25 the same day, seats 24D and 24E. Economy Special Saver. Driving to SFO and parking. Alan in 49D and 24D, Ever in 49E and 24E.

items.title: OMO3 Asakusa by Hoshino Resorts
items.summary: Booked. 1-15-5 Hanakawado.
items.detail: Eight nights. Thirteenth-floor lounge and a rooftop terrace facing Senso-ji and Tokyo Skytree. Everything on the Asakusa days is within a ten-minute walk of the door, and the Tobu and Tsukuba Express stations are both close.

items.title: Yayoi Kusama Museum
items.summary: The most at-risk item on the list. Check today.
items.detail: October tickets went on sale on 1 August, so they have been available for six weeks. The museum opens Thursday to Sunday only and sells 90-minute timed slots. Friday 23 is the single day of this trip that works, so if it is sold out the museum comes off the plan and Friday starts at Meiji Jingu instead. Buy for the 11:00 slot if it exists.

items.title: teamLab Planets
items.summary: Timed entry, on sale since late July.
items.detail: The whole of Thursday is built around this slot: Pigment at 13:00, Planets at about 15:30 for roughly two hours, then the Alvark game at 19:05 two Yurikamome stops away. Book the 15:30 entry or as near as you can get. Wear shorts, you go barefoot and there is shin-deep water.

items.title: Alvark Tokyo vs Ibaraki Robots
items.summary: Toyota Arena Tokyo, Aomi.
items.detail: Second night of the Alvark Entertainment Special 3DAYS. Adult seats were listing around 3,500 to 5,000 yen when sales opened. The arena is about five minutes' walk from Aomi on the Yurikamome, two stops back from Shin-Toyosu where Planets is. Halftime is a brass and dance quartet.

items.title: HIBIKUS taiko lesson
items.summary: Needs a human to write back, so start it now.
items.detail: This is a working taiko school under Miyamoto Unosuke in Nishi-Asakusa, not a tourist workshop, so the thing to confirm is that they will run a single visitor session for two people on the morning of Monday 19 October. Five minutes from the hotel and right by the Tsukuba Express station, which is why Monday runs Asakusa then Akihabara. If they cannot take you, the Oedo Sukeroku Taiko Dojo in Sotokanda runs explicit one and 1.5 hour traveller lessons in English and sits on the same Monday route, so the day does not change.

items.title: ZAKURO SHOW
items.summary: Buy the ticket and confirm the start time.
items.detail: Sixty minutes of taiko with koto, shamisen and shakuhachi, played a few feet away with English explanation. One minute from Meiji-jingumae exit 7. The start time decides Friday's running order: an evening show means Shibuya Sky at sunset first, an afternoon show means ZAKURO first and Shibuya Sky after dark. This is the only show of the trip now that the rock nights are off.

items.title: Kumihimo at DOMYO
items.summary: Book the morning; Tuesday is built behind it.
items.detail: Silk-cord braiding at a house founded in 1652, with English workshop plans. Kagurazaka station is on the Tozai line one stop before Iidabashi, so the morning slot feeds straight into the Koishikawa garden and then west to Nakano. Ask for the earliest session they run.

items.title: National Art Center, Louvre exhibition
items.summary: Timed exhibition ticket. The building is free, the show is not.
items.detail: Masterpieces of the Renaissance from the Musee du Louvre runs 9 September to 13 December 2026, with Leonardo's La Belle Ferronniere in Japan for the first time. The centre stays open until 20:00 on Saturdays for its own exhibitions, which is why it sits at the end of the Kapital day rather than the middle. Closed Tuesdays.

items.title: Mokuhankan Print Party
items.summary: Optional, but it fills far ahead, so decide now or not at all.
items.detail: Hands-on woodblock printing in English at David Bull's studio, five minutes from the hotel. It is the print counterpart to the film cameras and the sketchbooks, and it pairs with the original ukiyo-e at Ohya Shobo in Jimbocho on Monday. If you take it, it replaces Thursday's Yanaka walk rather than joining it.

items.title: Shibuya Sky, sunset slot
items.summary: Slots open about a month ahead. Watch from 23 September.
items.detail: The famous view, and the one thing on this list you cannot book yet. Sunset is about 16:55 in late October, so the 16:00 or 16:20 entries are the ones worth having and they go first. Friday already ends in Shibuya, so it costs no detour. If the sunset slots are gone, take a slot after dark, or fall back on the Hikarie Sky Lobby next door which is free and needs no booking.

items.title: Capyneko Cafe Kichijoji
items.summary: Reserve from about 6 October.
items.detail: The original Capyneko: free-roaming cats and a capybara in the same room. It sits between Nakano Broadway and the Gotoku-ji cat temple on the Tuesday run. If it will not take a booking, pignic cafe beside Inokashira Park is the alternative on the same street, with private rooms and a seasonal pig walk.

items.title: Otter cafe (Harry), Harajuku
items.summary: Reserve from about 9 October. This is the one you flagged.
items.detail: Otters, hedgehogs and chinchillas on Takeshita Street. Do one animal cafe on Friday, not three: there are eight within about 200 metres of each other and each one costs an hour of a day that already holds the denim strip, Five G, The Real McCoy's, two museums and the sunset.

items.title: Nezu Museum
items.summary: Check whether your date needs a timed ticket, and book if so.
items.detail: Kengo Kuma's building with a steep mossy garden of stone lanterns and teahouses, five minutes from Momotaro Aoyama and a few blocks from the Taro Okamoto studio. Closed Mondays, last entry 16:30. The garden needs the museum ticket.

items.title: Mizutani Camera, Ueno
items.summary: Confirm it exists and is open before building the morning around it.
items.detail: Reported as a secondhand camera and vintage watch dealer under a blue awning opposite Ueno station's south exit, English-speaking and tax-free registered. I could only confirm it through English travel writing, never a Japanese source or its own site, so treat every detail as unverified. If it does not hold up, Thursday's Okachimachi route still works on Quark Ueno and Hinoya.

items.title: United Arrows Harajuku
items.summary: Published addresses disagree and one listing reports a renovation closure.
items.detail: Both 3-28-1 and 2-31-12 Jingumae appear as the main store. Confirm the address and that it is trading before making the detour. The Roppongi Hills store on Saturday is the reliable one and sits two floors above the Kapital doors you are already visiting.

items.title: GoodWatch78, Nakano Broadway
items.summary: Short hours, roughly 13:00 to 18:00.
items.detail: Antique Rolex only, trading in parts and consignment, which is what makes it the likeliest place to find an Explorer as a bare head. Its hours are much shorter than the rest of the third floor, so confirm them and make it the first stop of the watch hunt rather than the last. Its site is served over plain http, so there is no link recorded in the guide.

items.title: The free places with awkward calendars
items.summary: No booking, but the closed days shape three different mornings.
items.detail: The Drum Museum is closed Mondays and Tuesdays and runs 11:00 to 16:00, which is why it sits on Sunday 18. The Edo Taito Traditional Crafts Center is free with weekend artisan demonstrations, which is why it anchors the departure morning. The Imperial Palace East Gardens close at 16:30 and are shut on Fridays, so Saturday is their only slot. Shinjuku Gyoen's last entry is 16:00 and it closes Mondays. Confirm all four against the October calendar.

items.title: Passports for tax-free
items.summary: Carry both. Used goods count.
items.detail: Tax-free applies to general goods over 5,000 yen for foreign visitors, and used goods are eligible, which matters for the vintage watches at Nakano and Ueno and for the denim. Bring both passports, not photocopies. Map Camera and the larger shops are registered; the small dealers vary, so ask before you commit.

items.title: Kamakura, the whole day
items.summary: JR on a Suica. No reservation, nothing books ahead.
items.detail: Leave the hotel by 7:30, Asakusa line to Shimbashi, Yokosuka line straight through to Kita-Kamakura by about 9:00. None of the eight temples and gardens takes a booking, and the Enoden is a tap-in. That flexibility is a large part of why Kamakura beat Nikko, which would have wanted reserved express seats.

items.title: The Asakusa doorstep
items.summary: All within a ten-minute walk, none of it bookable.
items.detail: Senso-ji, Nakamise, Kaminarimon, the free 8F deck at the Culture Center, Hoppy Street and the OMO3 rooftop. Onigiri Yadoroku opens late morning and sells out, so go early rather than book. Wanariya indigo dyeing takes walk-ins and runs about 45 minutes if a morning feels light.

items.title: Every shop on the list
items.summary: Just opening hours. Nakano Broadway does not wake up until noon.
items.detail: Kapital's six Tokyo doors, United Arrows, The Real McCoy's, the Harajuku denim strip, Five G and Echigoya, the Nakano and Ueno watch dealers, Itoya, Map Camera and Yodobashi, Sekaido, the Jimbocho book town. Two timing notes worth holding: most Nakano Broadway shops open at 12:00 and a few close Wednesdays, and the Jimbocho dealers mostly shut around 18:00 with many closed Sundays, so get there before 17:00 on Monday.
